PullRequest.Title: Merge conflicts: don't rescan the whole document after small edits
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

To find out whether a document has a conflict, `MergeConflictParser.containsConflict` joins the whole document into one string with `document.getText()` and searches it for `<<<<<<<` and `>>>>>>>`. The tracker runs it for every `getConflicts` call, which the decorator triggers after each edit.

This PR remembers, per `TextDocument`, the version at which the document was found to have no conflict. A change listener moves that version forward on single edits that insert no line break and can't have formed a marker. Markers have no line break, so a new one must overlap the inserted text or span the start of the change. Checking 6 characters on either side of the edit, on its line, is therefore enough; this also covers a deletion that joins two lines. All other edits fall back to the full check on the next request, as before:
- Enter and multi-line paste;
- several changes in one event (multi-cursor);
- more than 256 characters;
- reload from disk and line-ending changes.

No issue is associated; this came from profiling.

## Measured on my machine

Code OSS dev build: scrolling, typing and finding in a 47,000-line file without conflicts.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `getConflictsOrEmpty` | 545 ms | 5 ms |
| of which `getText` | 351 ms | 5 ms |

## Why it is safe

- A remembered version only matches when it equals the document's current version. Versions only increase, so an older record can never match. If events skip a version, the optimization is lost for that edit, but no conflict is missed.
- The record is a `WeakMap` keyed by the document object. A document that is closed and reopened is a new object.
- A randomized check of 500,000 single edits built from partial and full markers found no edit that formed a marker without being flagged. The edits included deletions that join lines, and inserting `<` next to `<<<<<<`. A margin of 5 characters instead of 6 fails that check.

## How to test

This extension has no unit tests, so I checked the behavior in a running Code OSS, with the same scripted steps before and after the change:

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Open a file that already has a conflict | code lens appears after 422 ms | after 435 ms |
| Open a clean 200-line file | no code lens | no code lens |
| Type a conflict block into the clean file, line by line | code lens appears after 411 ms | after 408 ms |
| Delete the block line by line with Cmd+Shift+K | code lens goes away after 408 ms | after 409 ms |
| Type the `=======` and `>>>>>>>` lines first, then the `<<<<<<<` line | code lens appears after 409 ms | after 412 ms |

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p extensions/merge-conflict/tsconfig.json` | passed |
| `pnpm run oxlint extensions/merge-conflict/src/documentTracker.ts extensions/merge-conflict/src/mergeConflictParser.ts` | passed |

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Edit-triggered conflict queries repeatedly materialize and search an entire conflict-free document. Pending consumers are coalesced per URI, but completed negative results are not retained. For E edited versions actually scanned and D document characters, the old path performs O(E*D) whole-document work; the model's string cache only avoids another join within the same unchanged version.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Strongly evidenced synchronous extension-host CPU and document-sized string allocation after small edits in large conflict-free files, delaying decoration/code-lens completion and other extension-host work. This is static call-path evidence, not an independently reproduced timing measurement.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Caches the conflict-free result per TextDocument and version, and preserves it across single edits of at most 256 inserted characters with no newline when the bounded marker neighborhood is safe. Warm requests avoid whole-document materialization and searching; unsupported edits or possible markers retain the existing full-check fallback.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base getConflictsOrEmpty unconditionally calls MergeConflictParser.containsConflict (base documentTracker.ts:119) before returning an empty result. MergeDecorator.begin subscribes to document changes and applyDecorations awaits tracker.getConflicts for visible editors (mergeDecorator.ts:34-35, 178). The per-URI Delayer coalesces pending requests, but documentTracker.ts:83 removes each completed task, so subsequent edit-triggered tasks repeat the check. containsConflict calls document.getText and searches the document-sized string (mergeConflictParser.ts:150-151). ExtHostDocumentData delegates getText to MirrorTextModel, whose getText joins all lines when its string cache is empty and whose onEvents invalidates that cache on every model change (mirrorTextModel.ts:84-107). The added version check at documentTracker.ts:128 returns before this work; the added listener advances the negative-cache version for eligible marker-free edits.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial conflict detection and small edits in a visible conflict-free document
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Activation occurs onStartupFinished. Decorations and code lenses await getConflicts; scans run synchronously on the extension-host thread after the existing zero-delay timer. The new change listener runs before the consumers registered by ServiceWrapper and maintains the negative-cache version synchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize a full document string with lines.join and search for conflict markers in memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: one materialization per edited version actually queried, unless another consumer already materialized it; marker searches repeat per completed scan task. After: one cold check, then zero full checks across eligible marker-free edits and repeated warm queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full-document operation ran after every completed-task cache miss; the diff removes its repeated execution on the warm negative path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous work must finish before getConflicts resolves and feature consumers proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero renderer calls for already-empty keys because ExtHostTextEditor suppresses no-op clears. On transition from conflicts to no conflicts, at most one clear per previously populated decoration key per editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical empty-decoration suppression and clearing behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Issued only after the scan resolves; renderer completion is not awaited by applyDecorations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the existing setContext command with the conflict count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical command per code-lens provision, not per line or conflict.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command was issued per provision.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Issued after detection; the provider does not await this command.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: D document characters, E eligible edit events, and V visible editors showing the document. Pending consumers share one scan task per URI; the decorator also suppresses overlapping updates per editor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One tracker service and one new change subscription. Pending scan requests coalesce per URI through Delayer; local scans execute serially on the extension-host event loop. Decoration work is additionally guarded per editor.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold requests still materialize/search the document and record a conflict-free version. Warm requests at that version return immediately. Single edits with at most 256 inserted characters, no newline, and no nearby start/end marker advance the cached version. The marker slice contains at most 268 characters. lineAt returns a wrapper referencing an existing mirrored line, without eagerly calculating whitespace or crossing IPC. MirrorTextModel already caches the full text within an unchanged version, but invalidates it on each model event.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the edit subscription, consumer awaits, per-URI coalescing, mirror string-cache invalidation, and negative-cache fast path were traced in source.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Document sizes and edit rates vary; no timings were independently measured. The new listener performs bounded marker checks rather than a document-size scan.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. This scenario removes repeated whole-document CPU/allocation work; a regression-fix learning signal was submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Newline, multi-cursor, large-paste, reload, or possible-marker edits; documents containing conflicts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The next decoration/code-lens or command query must finish the existing full containsConflict check. If both marker types exist, scanDocument walks document lines and constructs descriptors before consumers proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Full text materialization/marker search followed, when markers are present, by a line-by-line conflict scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full check per coalesced scan task; the joined string is reused within the same model version. At most one line scan per task when both marker types are found.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same operations and same pending-task coalescing; negative repeated queries can now skip the full check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks feature-query completion on the extension-host thread.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and send grouped decoration ranges to the renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to seven populated decoration-type groups per editor per update, with range payload proportional to C+A; not one IPC per conflict.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Issued after conflict detection; acknowledgments are not awaited here.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing telemetry reporter submission for a document observed with markers; outbound transport is SDK-owned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one report per URI over tracker lifetime, using the unchanged seenDocumentsWithConflicts set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same report, payload, and once-per-URI guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reporter submission occurs during the scan; network completion is not awaited by this code.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: D characters, L lines, C conflicts, A common-ancestor regions, and V visible editors. Edits unsupported by the incremental predicate invalidate the effective negative-cache match rather than fan out work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pending consumers still coalesce into one task per URI. Line scans remain synchronous and serial in the extension host. Decoration RPCs are grouped by decoration type, not by conflict.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Multiple changes, text longer than 256 characters, and inserted newlines immediately take the conservative fallback. Possible markers also prevent advancing the negative version. A subsequent negative full check establishes the new cache version. Positive results are not persistently cached, exactly as before. Version gaps cannot match the previous negative record.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for conservative fallback, full-scan cardinality, range grouping, and unchanged telemetry ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large/conflicted documents retain their previous scan costs. Actual SDK transport timing is outside the inspected repository call path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression: fallback and positive-document work were preserved, not newly introduced or amplified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edits to previously checked hidden documents, feature disabling, close/reopen, and extension disposal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new workspace listener runs during document-change dispatch, even without an active consumer, but only invokes the bounded predicate for a document whose cached version is exactly the preceding version. Hidden-document edits otherwise need no merge-conflict query to proceed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: E document-change events across live documents; one number retained per negatively checked TextDocument, not per historical version or edit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One service-wide listener, no per-document subscriptions or spawned work. It is disposed by tracker.dispose; ServiceWrapper disposal is owned by the extension context.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: WeakMap keys do not keep closed documents alive; reopening uses another document object. The cache stores only the latest negative version. Documents never checked, or with unmatched versions, take only the constant-time map/version guard. Feature disabling leaves the listener active but does not turn it into a full scan.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: WeakMap ownership, bounded input guards, the single service construction, and explicit listener disposal are visible in the changed code and service lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The additional constant/bounded work can occur for background edits, but no collection-sized traversal, retained document ownership, or external operation was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable eager-work or retention regression. The new listener has bounded local work and an explicit disposal path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Conflict navigation, accepting changes, and accepting all conflicts across selected resources
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor commands await conflict queries before choosing ranges. Multi-resource acceptance first awaits Promise.all of document opens, then queries documents sequentially, constructs one WorkspaceEdit, and submits it. These ordering points are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: U cold distinct-URI opens, zero for documents already in the extension-host document map; repeated in-flight URI requests share a promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical Promise.all fan-out and loaded/in-flight document caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All requested opens must finish before the multi-resource scan loop begins.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve cold file-backed document models using the existing text-file service; remote/virtual schemes use their existing providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold model-resolution operation per distinct uncached resource, subject to existing model reuse; no read per conflict.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same resource resolution path and resource cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold file resolution is upstream of conflict scanning and workspace-edit construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and apply conflict replacements through one editor edit or one workspace edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One edit RPC for a nonempty editor batch; one workspace-edit submission for the resource command, carrying C replacements. Existing no-op editor edits avoid RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same batching, payload scale, and await placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Editor accept-all awaits edit completion. The multi-resource method submits its workspace edit without awaiting completion, unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update selection and reveal the selected conflict for navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selection update and one reveal per successful navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Issued after the conflict query; no extra detection boundary is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R selected URIs, U distinct uncached URIs after document-loader deduplication, and total C conflict replacements. Documents already loaded produce no open RPC; scans are per document rather than per conflict.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Open requests use existing Promise.all with per-URI loader coalescing and no new global limit. The command's document-query loop is serial. Conflict replacements are batched into one editor edit or one workspace edit.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ExtHostDocuments returns loaded documents immediately and coalesces in-flight opens by URI. Negative conflict versions can now bypass repeated scans. Positive scans and tracker.forget calls retain existing behavior; subsequent document versions make old negative entries inapplicable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: opened-document caching, per-URI coalescing, sequential conflict queries, and edit batching were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The existing cold-open burst may be large for many resources, but the diff neither increases it nor changes scheduling. Remote-provider costs vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced boundary fan-out or concurrency regression. Existing command I/O and IPC counts are unchanged; negative queries become cheaper.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compare current and incoming conflict contents
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Compare awaits conflict detection, encodes conflict ranges into two virtual URIs, and invokes vscode.diff. Each content provider obtains the original document and builds one side's text before the diff can display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON-encode all conflict ranges into current/incoming virtual-document URI queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two encodings with payload proportional to C.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical range metadata and two encodings.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke vscode.diff and, for the Below preference, the existing new-editor-group command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical diff command and optionally one group command per compare invocation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read source ranges from the local mirror and concatenate the virtual side's complete text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two range reads per conflict plus one trailing range per side; output proportional to D. Source opens use the existing loaded/in-flight document cache and normally add zero source-open IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical full-side reconstruction and range-read count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each virtual side must be constructed before its content is available to the diff editor.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: C conflict ranges and D source characters, with two virtual document sides. The source is normally already open; concurrent cold requests for its URI share the document loader.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The compare command's existing awaits are sequential. The workbench may request both content sides independently; shared source loading is coalesced per URI. No new tasks or boundaries are added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Positive conflict scanning remains unchanged. Source openTextDocument calls normally hit the existing document cache. The new negative cache does not alter range metadata, virtual URI keys, or content reconstruction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: neither serialization payloads nor content-provider behavior changed, and their consumers were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large conflict sets retain their existing JSON and content-allocation costs; no profiling was performed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The diff only changes upstream negative detection, not positive compare costs.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the complete two-file inventory and both full diff pages. Traced callers, model string caching, scheduling, service ownership, decoration no-op suppression, command/document I/O, and compare serialization. No actionable high-confidence diff-introduced performance findings. Recorded one concrete repeated-work regression fix with base-line blame provenance. Static read-only review; no measured timings claimed.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
